title: SPROUTS FARMERS MARKET
intro:
All grocery stores use the word “fresh” in their marketing. So how could Sprouts Farmers Market connect their brand to delicious, fresh food and not be just another bland grocery store?

Our solution paired fresh imagery with a fresh attitude. We embraced Sprouts’ “forager spirit”—a sense of discovery—to make freshness exciting, inspiring, and energizing. While competitors simply claimed to be fresh, Sprouts could own it through an invigorating sense of discovery and possibility.

title: CORITA ART CENTER
intro:
Corita Art Center preserves and promotes the art, teachings, and enduring commitment to social justice of pop artist Corita Kent. The center is always looking to bring awareness of her life and work to new audiences.

The challenge: honor her spirit without copying her style. Across social assets, gallery materials, merchandise, and a benefit-dinner zine, I drew on her process, philosophy and rules. Rule nine set the tone: “Be happy whenever you can manage it. Enjoy yourself. It’s lighter than you think.” That sense of joy and lightness informed the work across each application.

I’m happy to report that my break bread zine design won first place at the 2026 PRINT Awards for best brochure. More information about the zine and award can be found [here](https://www.printmag.com/awards/print-awards-2026-honoring-the-work-that-stands-apart/).

title: SoCAL EARTH
intro:
SoCal Earth is an environmental data program created by the Robert Redford Conservancy. The conservancy asked me to develop a visual identity for the program’s initial website launch—one that would appeal to Southern Californians while expressing resourcefulness through design.

To turn the abstract idea of “resourcefulness” into something tangible, I started with what I had in my studio: loose construction paper. My cut-paper logos and illustrations put the program’s philosophy into practice—use what’s already available. I digitized and refined the collages and pencil drawings into website graphics, including Ollie, a burrowing owl mascot for children. All handmade. All for the environment. To get the full experience, visit socalearth.org

title: CULTURAL OLYMPIAD POSTER
intro:
In spring 2024, I entered the Paris Cultural Olympiad student competition. The brief: create a poster and animation connecting the Paris 2024 Olympics to Los Angeles 2028.

The connection was hiding in plain sight at the cheap souvenir shops you see in these cities. A plastic Eiffel Tower and a faux Academy Award were elevated to symbols of civic pride. Using a unifying mid-century cut-paper style, I combined these icons into a poster that visualized the transition from Paris to Los Angeles.

title: VALLEY STRONG CREDIT UNION
intro:
The ask was simple: Help us write more loans. The challenge was that the loan process can make customers feel nervous, anxious, or disengaged.
So why not reframe that anxiety as anticipation? After all, a home loan is also the path to a new house.

The visual identity took shape around houses of every size—short, tall, and wide. Minimal forms invited people to imagine themselves in these new spaces, while Valley Strong Credit Union’s green palette grounded the system in the brand. Through a light and uplifting tone, the identity transformed a home loan from a source of anxiety into a path toward an exciting future.

title: More Work
intro: This page contains various other projects, including my ArtCenter Graduate Graphic Design thesis, Forced Perspective: An Exhibit on Brand. This thesis explored how branding shapes our understanding of the world. I created original artwork and an exhibition, then documented the project in a 300-page book. This and other internship and student design work can be seen below.
